prompt: What is a VMkernel network adapter?
options: An IP-enabled network interface used by the ESXi host
A virtual disk attached to a guest
A guest operating system’s network adapter
A DNS zone containing ESXi names
en: VMkernel interfaces support host networking, distinct from guest vNICs.
ru: VMkernel interface host networking ke liye hai, guest vNIC se alag.

prompt: Which naming pattern normally identifies VMkernel interfaces?
options: vmk0, vmk1 and other vmk numbers
vmnic0 and vmnic1 only
Hard Disk 1 and Hard Disk 2
VCPLAB.Com and in-addr.arpa
en: vmk identifies a VMkernel interface; vmnic identifies an ESXi network adapter.
ru: vmk VMkernel interface aur vmnic ESXi network adapter ko identify karta hai.

prompt: Which object carries the ESXi management address in this lab?
options: vmk0
The vSwitch0 label itself
The guest VM’s CNAME record
The datastore name
en: The host IP endpoint is its VMkernel interface, not the switch name.
ru: Host IP endpoint VMkernel interface hai, switch name nahin.

prompt: Which statement about vMotion is accurate?
options: It is a function that uses appropriately configured VMkernel networking
It is another name for every VMkernel adapter
Creating any vmk automatically performs a migration
It is a guest-only DNS protocol
en: A VMkernel interface and the service using it are different concepts.
ru: VMkernel interface aur usay use karne wali service alag concepts hain.

prompt: Does creating a storage VMkernel interface automatically mount an NFS datastore?
options: No; target, protocol and datastore configuration/testing remain separate
Yes; the STORAGE label mounts every available export
Yes; all reachable disks are formatted automatically
Only if the address begins with 172.16
en: Network configuration does not complete storage-protocol or datastore setup.
ru: Network configuration storage-protocol ya datastore setup complete nahin karti.

prompt: What is the key difference between a VMkernel interface and its port group?
options: The interface supplies the host IP endpoint; the group supplies network attachment/policy context
Both are identical names for one DNS record
The group is a disk; the interface is a CPU
The group assigns every guest its administrator password
en: Separate networking objects provide addressing and connection-policy roles.
ru: Alag networking objects addressing aur connection-policy roles dete hain.

prompt: When does reaching an off-subnet storage IP require routing?
options: When the destination is not reachable through a suitable directly connected subnet
Never; every storage label creates a route
Only when a DNS alias is uppercase
Only when the guest uses a split virtual disk
en: Off-subnet reachability needs an appropriate route and working path.
ru: Off-subnet reachability ko munasib route aur working path chahiye.

prompt: What does MTU describe?
options: The maximum packet size supported at a network layer on an interface/path
The guaranteed application throughput
The number of VMs allowed on a datastore
The time before a DNS record expires
en: MTU is a size parameter; it is not a bandwidth guarantee.
ru: MTU size parameter hai, bandwidth guarantee nahin.

prompt: What must be considered before using jumbo frames for IP storage?
options: Compatible MTU and successful testing across the entire path
Only changing the VMkernel MTU on one end
Only renaming the port group JUMBO
Only adding another DNS suffix
en: A larger MTU must work across the relevant virtual and physical network path.
ru: Bara MTU relevant virtual aur physical poore path par work karna chahiye.

prompt: Why specify an interface in vmkping?
options: To test connectivity using the intended VMkernel path
To create a new interface automatically
To install an iSCSI target
To guarantee datastore read/write performance
en: Interface selection helps avoid testing the wrong host network.
ru: Interface selection ghalat host network test karne se bachati hai.

prompt: Which address was recorded for management vmk0 on desktop-esxi9?
en: The ESXi9 management checkpoint uses .10; .11 belongs to the separate ESXi8 context.
ru: ESXi9 management checkpoint .10 hai; .11 alag ESXi8 context hai.

prompt: Which storage VMkernel address and prefix were captured in the original storage setup?
en: The recorded STORAGE interface was 172.16.0.102 with mask 255.255.0.0.
ru: Recorded STORAGE interface 172.16.0.102 aur mask 255.255.0.0 tha.

prompt: Which combination was shown after the original storage-network creation?
options: vSwitch1 → STORAGE → vmk1
vSwitch0 → SERVERS → every guest automatically
DNS01 → VCPLAB.Com → an NFS export
VMnet2 → a new AD domain
en: The captured storage network consisted of those host networking objects.
ru: Captured storage network un host networking objects par mushtamil tha.

prompt: What MTU was captured in the storage wizard?
options: 9000 as a verified end-to-end result
65535 as a measured storage rate
en: 1500 was the recorded baseline; jumbo-frame success was not documented.
ru: 1500 recorded baseline tha; jumbo-frame success documented nahin.

prompt: The storage service checkboxes are not selected in the captured properties. Which claim is justified?
options: Those screenshots do not establish enabled vMotion/vSAN services or mounted storage
Every storage protocol is permanently impossible
A datastore was mounted automatically
The interface has no possible IP connectivity
en: Service enablement and protocol/storage completion require their own evidence.
ru: Service enablement aur protocol/storage completion ki evidence alag chahiye.

prompt: A same-subnet storage peer is to be tested while management uses gateway 10.0.0.1. What should not be done merely to match the storage label?
options: Replace the management default gateway with an invented storage gateway
Inspect the actual routes
Verify the intended peer address
Select the correct interface for testing
en: Do not disrupt the existing default route simply because another connected subnet is added.
ru: Doosri connected subnet add honay par existing default route ko bila wajah disturb na karein.

prompt: A later exercise proposes 172.16.50.0/24 while existing STORAGE is 172.16.0.102/16. What is the planning concern?
options: The proposed /24 overlaps the existing /16 connected network
Different third octets guarantee no overlap
Both are public address ranges that cannot be used privately
The overlap is removed by changing a port-group label

prompt: Which read-only command displays VMkernel IPv4 address settings?
options: esxcli network ip interface ipv4 get
esxcli network nic list
esxcli storage filesystem unmount
esxcli system shutdown poweroff
en: The IP-interface command inspects host interface addressing.
ru: IP-interface command host interface addressing inspect karti hai.

prompt: Which command inspects IPv4 routes on ESXi?
options: esxcli network ip route ipv4 list
esxcli network ip dns server list
esxcli network nic get -n vmnic0
esxcli storage filesystem list
en: Routes describe destination reachability decisions, distinct from DNS servers or NIC link data.
ru: Routes destination reachability decisions batate hain; DNS servers aur NIC link data alag hain.

prompt: A known storage peer replies to vmkping through the intended storage vmk. What is established?
options: Basic IP reachability on that tested path
A verified mounted datastore and successful storage I/O
Guaranteed throughput at the NIC’s reported link rate
Proof that every storage protocol is enabled
en: A ping is a reachability test, not storage-session or I/O verification.
ru: Ping reachability test hai, storage-session ya I/O verification nahin.

prompt: The intended storage peer does not reply. Which checks are most relevant?
options: Correct vmk, IP/mask, VLAN, uplink mapping, peer firewall and route where needed
Only the name of the VM storage folder
Only the Windows wallpaper
Only the capitalization of the STORAGE label
en: Investigate the actual network path and endpoint, not labels alone.
ru: Actual network path aur endpoint investigate hon, sirf labels nahin.

prompt: A ping works without an explicit interface, but the storage path is in doubt. What is useful next?
options: Repeat with the actual intended VMkernel interface and inspect routes
Assume all interfaces have been tested
Delete vmk0 immediately
Change the peer’s DNS suffix instead
en: A successful default-path test may not exercise the intended storage interface.
ru: Successful default-path test intended storage interface ko exercise nahin bhi kar sakta.

prompt: A new VMkernel interface is assigned a different number than the notes’ vmk2 example. What should be used in tests?
options: The actual assigned interface number from the current inventory
Always vmk2 regardless of inventory
Always vmk0 because it was created first
The uplink’s vmnic number as the vmk name
en: Interface numbers must come from the current host, not an assumed example.
ru: Interface numbers current host se lene hain, assumed example se nahin.

prompt: Small-packet reachability works, but a planned jumbo-frame validation fails. What should be investigated?
options: MTU consistency and supported packet size across the full path
Only whether the port group is named STORAGE
Assume any successful small ping proves jumbo support
Delete reverse DNS records first
en: Small packets do not establish that the path can carry jumbo frames.
ru: Small packets se path ki jumbo frames carry karne ki ability prove nahin hoti.

prompt: Management access disappears after a VMkernel change. Which response best preserves recovery?
options: Use the local console to inspect and restore recorded management settings
Reset every network object before identifying the change
Delete the storage datastore immediately
Assume the DNS suffix must be changed first
en: Console access and known previous configuration help recover without broad destructive changes.
ru: Console access aur known previous configuration broad destructive changes ke baghair recovery mein madad karte hain.
